item.text: I’ll trace the audit event checker and authentication gRPC server wiring, record the checkpoint first, then implement the token event support and run the relevant existing tests.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "mkdir -p .codex-role-output && cat > .codex-role-output/checkpoint.md <<'EOF'
# Checkpoint

Task: Add audit logging support for token creation and deletion events.

Plan:
- Inspect repository guidance and locate the audit event checker and gRPC initialization.
- Update token resource/event mappings and token-deletion configuration flow.
- Run relevant existing tests and review the final diff.
EOF
pwd && rg --files -g 'AGENTS.md' -g '"'!vendor'"' -g '"'!node_modules'"' -g '"'!dist'"' | head -80 && git status --short && rg -n \"audit|Audit|tokenDeleted|token:[REDACTED_SECRET]" --glob '"'!vendor/**'"' --glob '"'!node_modules/**'"' | head -240"

./internal/server/audit/README.md:3:Audit Events are pieces of data that describe a particular thing that has happened in a system. At Flipt, we provide the functionality of processing and batching these audit events and an abstraction for sending these audit events to a sink.

./internal/server/audit/README.md:28:Any combination of the above nouns and verbs can be used to filter audit events. For example, `flag:created` would filter audit events for only `created` events for `flags`.
./internal/server/audit/README.md:30:You may also use the `*` wildcard to filter on all nouns or verbs. For example, `*:created` would filter audit events for only `created` events for all nouns.
./internal/server/audit/README.md:32:Similarly, `flag:*` would filter audit events for all verbs for `flags`.
./internal/server/audit/README.md:34:Finally, `*:*` would filter audit events for all nouns and verbs which is the default behavior.
